description: Read-only CARLA exporter monitoring. Select a Prometheus datasource, scrape job and exporter instance. Vehicle role and actor filters apply only to vehicle panels. No data means unavailable telemetry, not a measured zero.

panels.description: Current health and world summary for one selected exporter instance.
panels.title: Overview

panels.description: 1 means the required CARLA RPC reads and response validation succeeded in this collection; 0 means they failed. This is separate from exporter HTTP availability and world-stream connectivity.
panels.title: CARLA RPC

panels.description: 1 means the world-state TCP stream is established; 0 means it is disconnected. A connected stream does not prove new frames are arriving. Check Frame age and Simulation FPS.
panels.title: World stream

panels.description: Wall-clock time since the exporter last observed a new frame, measured with a monotonic clock. Colors mark inactivity at 1 s and 5 s; they are visual defaults, not alert rules. A synchronous simulation may intentionally wait for a tick.
panels.title: Frame age

panels.description: Simulation frame advancement per wall-clock second over --performance.window (default 10 s), including idle time. This is simulation FPS, not rendering FPS. Data is absent until a valid observation window is available.
panels.title: Simulation FPS

panels.description: Simulation seconds advanced per wall-clock second over --performance.window. 1x means real time, 0.5x means half speed, and 2x means double speed. Zero indicates no observed progress; it does not explain why.
panels.title: Real-time factor

panels.description: Vehicle count in the last validated world snapshot, before exporter vehicle filters or dashboard role/actor filters. It can exceed the number of vehicles whose telemetry is displayed.
panels.title: Vehicles

panels.description: Observed FPS uses the exporter's rolling performance window. The dashed real-time reference is 1 / fixed_delta_seconds: with a 0.05 s step, 20 FPS gives a real-time factor of 1. It is not an enforced FPS limit and is hidden for variable time steps.
panels.title: Frame rate

panels.description: Simulation time divided by wall-clock time, including idle time in the exporter's performance window. The reference at 1x indicates real time; it is not a workload-specific performance objective.
panels.title: Simulation pace

panels.description: History of Prometheus scrape success, required CARLA RPC reads, and world-stream connectivity. These signals describe different connections; none alone proves frame progress. Missing data is kept as a gap.
panels.title: Connection history

panels.description: Seconds since the last newly observed frame. Increasing age with a connected stream means frames are not advancing. Intentional pauses and clients withholding ticks in synchronous mode can produce the same pattern as a fault.
panels.title: Frame freshness

panels.description: Map name and CARLA server version from the latest successful collection. Coordinates are expressed in this map's world frame. The information metric has value 1; its labels carry the metadata.
panels.title: World

panels.description: Current actor counts by blueprint category, summed across lifecycle states. Counts cover the validated world snapshot and ignore vehicle filters. Each bar shows an absolute count; bar length is relative to the largest category.
panels.title: Actors · current

panels.description: Last observed CARLA simulation frame number. It belongs to the current world/episode and may reset after reloading the world or restarting the server. It is not a lifetime counter.
panels.title: Frame number

panels.description: Simulation seconds elapsed since the current CARLA episode began. This is simulation time, not wall-clock server uptime; it may reset when the episode changes.
panels.title: Simulation elapsed

panels.description: Exporter-host Unix timestamp when a new world frame was last received, displayed in the dashboard timezone. It depends on the exporter host's clock. Frame age is the monotonic measure for inactivity.
panels.title: Last snapshot received

panels.description: Frame advancement accumulated during this exporter process. Initial frame numbers and reconnect gaps are excluded; a new episode does not subtract previous progress. The counter resets when the exporter restarts.
panels.title: Frames observed

panels.description: Simulation-time advancement accumulated during this exporter process. Initial elapsed time and reconnect gaps are excluded. The counter resets when the exporter restarts; it differs from elapsed time in the current CARLA episode.
panels.title: Simulation observed

panels.description: SYNCHRONOUS means CARLA waits for a client tick to advance. ASYNCHRONOUS means the server advances independently. The exporter only reads this setting and never sends ticks.
panels.title: Synchronous mode

panels.description: ENABLED means CARLA rendering is active; DISABLED means no_rendering_mode is set. Rendering settings affect workloads and sensor output, so interpret FPS together with this mode.
panels.title: Rendering mode

panels.description: Whether CARLA physics substepping is enabled. Substeps divide simulation frames for physics integration; they do not represent additional world frames or an independent FPS target.
panels.title: Physics substepping

panels.description: Configured simulation time advanced per frame. Zero means a variable time step. A fixed step defines simulation time, not how long a frame takes to compute in wall-clock time.
panels.title: Fixed step

panels.description: Configured maximum physics substep duration, in simulation seconds. This is a settings limit, not a measurement of actual physics execution time.
panels.title: Max physics substep

panels.description: Configured maximum number of physics substeps per world frame. When substepping is enabled, fixed_delta_seconds should fit within max_substep_delta_seconds multiplied by max_substeps.
panels.title: Max physics substeps

panels.description: The last observed frame's simulation delta compared with configured fixed-step and physics-substep limits. All values are simulation seconds; they do not measure CPU or GPU processing duration.
panels.title: Simulation step

panels.description: Estimated frame-counter increase over the selected dashboard time range. Prometheus increase() handles resets and extrapolates at the range boundaries, so the result is rounded for display. Initial values and unobserved reconnect gaps are excluded. At least two samples are required.
panels.title: Frames advanced · selected range

panels.description: Estimated simulation-time increase over the selected dashboard time range. Prometheus increase() handles resets and extrapolates at the boundaries. This is simulated duration, not wall-clock duration; at least two samples are required.
panels.title: Simulation advanced · selected range

panels.description: History of actor counts by blueprint category, summed across lifecycle states. Includes the entire validated world snapshot regardless of vehicle role/actor filters. Missing telemetry is not converted to zero.
panels.title: Actors by kind

panels.description: History of actor counts aggregated across categories by CARLA lifecycle state: active, dormant, pending_kill, invalid, or unknown. These are actor lifecycle states, not vehicle driving states.
panels.title: Actor lifecycle states

panels.description: Vehicles present in the latest validated snapshot after both exporter-side filters and dashboard role/actor filters. Role names need not be unique. Actor IDs are scoped to an episode and may be reused after a world reset.

targets.expr: carla_vehicle_present{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",actor_id=~"${actor:regex}"} * on (job, instance, episode_id, actor_id) group_left(role_name, blueprint_id) carla_vehicle_info{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",role_name=~"${role:regex}"}

panels.title: Vehicle inventory

panels.description: Magnitude of the vehicle's 3D world velocity, in meters per second. It includes the vertical component and is unsigned. Stationary vehicles can report very small numerical motion.

targets.expr: carla_vehicle_speed_meters_per_second{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",actor_id=~"${actor:regex}"} * on (job, instance, episode_id, actor_id) group_left(role_name, blueprint_id) carla_vehicle_info{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",role_name=~"${role:regex}"}

panels.title: Speed

panels.description: PRESENT means the vehicle was in the validated snapshot. The exporter emits value 1 and removes the series when the vehicle disappears; it does not emit a persistent zero. Gaps can also mean unavailable telemetry.

targets.expr: carla_vehicle_present{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",actor_id=~"${actor:regex}"} * on (job, instance, episode_id, actor_id) group_left(role_name, blueprint_id) carla_vehicle_info{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",role_name=~"${role:regex}"}

panels.title: Vehicle presence

panels.description: Last applied throttle command, normalized from 0 to 1 and displayed as a percentage. It is a control input, not measured engine output or acceleration.

targets.expr: carla_vehicle_control_throttle_ratio{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",actor_id=~"${actor:regex}"} * on (job, instance, episode_id, actor_id) group_left(role_name, blueprint_id) carla_vehicle_info{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",role_name=~"${role:regex}"}

panels.title: Throttle

panels.description: Last applied brake command, normalized from 0 to 1 and displayed as a percentage. It is a control input; vehicle deceleration also depends on physics and other conditions.

targets.expr: carla_vehicle_control_brake_ratio{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",actor_id=~"${actor:regex}"} * on (job, instance, episode_id, actor_id) group_left(role_name, blueprint_id) carla_vehicle_info{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",role_name=~"${role:regex}"}

panels.title: Brake

panels.description: Last applied normalized steering command from -1 to 1. This is not a steering-wheel or road-wheel angle in radians. The resulting turn depends on the vehicle model and physics.

targets.expr: carla_vehicle_control_steer{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",actor_id=~"${actor:regex}"} * on (job, instance, episode_id, actor_id) group_left(role_name, blueprint_id) carla_vehicle_info{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",role_name=~"${role:regex}"}

panels.title: Steering command

panels.description: Sampled positions over the selected period in the CARLA world frame: +X points right on this plot and +Y points up. CARLA uses a left-handed, Z-up frame. Map viewers may flip or rotate their screen axes, so visual orientation is not guaranteed to match a map image. Axes autoscale independently; pixel distances are not a map scale. Sampling follows the scrape interval and query resolution, not every simulation frame. Points are kept separate by job, instance, episode and actor.

targets.expr: carla_vehicle_position_meters{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",actor_id=~"${actor:regex}",axis=~"x|y"} * on (job, instance, episode_id, actor_id) group_left(role_name, blueprint_id) carla_vehicle_info{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",role_name=~"${role:regex}"}

panels.title: Vehicle positions · XY

panels.description: Latest sampled X/Y/Z in the CARLA map's world frame, in meters. Values are unmodified exporter coordinates; Z is height, not distance from the road surface. Empty cells mean missing values. Screen orientation in a map viewer does not change these coordinates. Z trend shows the selected-period height history alongside the latest values. Sparkline scales are automatic; use the numeric Z column for absolute height. Historical actors without current X/Y samples are omitted.

targets.expr: carla_vehicle_position_meters{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",actor_id=~"${actor:regex}"} * on (job, instance, episode_id, actor_id) group_left(role_name, blueprint_id) carla_vehicle_info{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",role_name=~"${role:regex}"}

carla_vehicle_position_meters{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",actor_id=~"${actor:regex}",axis="z"} * on (job, instance, episode_id, actor_id) group_left(role_name, blueprint_id) carla_vehicle_info{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",role_name=~"${role:regex}"}

panels.title: Coordinates · current

panels.description: Vehicle yaw in radians in CARLA's left-handed coordinate convention. Zero aligns with world +X; positive yaw turns toward +Y. Crossing the angle wrap boundary can appear as a jump and does not imply an instantaneous full turn.

targets.expr: carla_vehicle_yaw_radians{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",actor_id=~"${actor:regex}"} * on (job, instance, episode_id, actor_id) group_left(role_name, blueprint_id) carla_vehicle_info{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",role_name=~"${role:regex}"}

panels.title: Yaw

panels.description: Gear in the last applied control: negative is reverse, zero is neutral, and positive values are forward gears. It is not a measured speed or proof of movement.

targets.expr: carla_vehicle_control_gear{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",actor_id=~"${actor:regex}"} * on (job, instance, episode_id, actor_id) group_left(role_name, blueprint_id) carla_vehicle_info{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",role_name=~"${role:regex}"}

panels.title: Gear

panels.description: Velocity components along the fixed CARLA world X/Y/Z axes, in meters per second. These are not vehicle-relative forward/lateral velocities; signs indicate axis direction.

targets.expr: carla_vehicle_velocity_meters_per_second{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",actor_id=~"${actor:regex}"} * on (job, instance, episode_id, actor_id) group_left(role_name, blueprint_id) carla_vehicle_info{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",role_name=~"${role:regex}"}

panels.title: Velocity components

panels.description: Acceleration components along CARLA world X/Y/Z, in meters per second squared. These are world-frame values, not a passenger comfort or body-frame longitudinal acceleration measurement.

targets.expr: carla_vehicle_acceleration_meters_per_second_squared{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",actor_id=~"${actor:regex}"} * on (job, instance, episode_id, actor_id) group_left(role_name, blueprint_id) carla_vehicle_info{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",role_name=~"${role:regex}"}

panels.title: Acceleration components

panels.description: Angular velocity components about CARLA world X/Y/Z axes, in radians per second. These are rotation rates, separate from yaw angle and steering command.

targets.expr: carla_vehicle_angular_velocity_radians_per_second{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",actor_id=~"${actor:regex}"} * on (job, instance, episode_id, actor_id) group_left(role_name, blueprint_id) carla_vehicle_info{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",role_name=~"${role:regex}"}

panels.title: Angular velocity

panels.description: Hand-brake and reverse flags from the last applied control. ON/OFF shows requested control state. Reverse being ON does not prove the vehicle is currently moving backward.

targets.expr: carla_vehicle_control_hand_brake{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",actor_id=~"${actor:regex}"} * on (job, instance, episode_id, actor_id) group_left(role_name, blueprint_id) carla_vehicle_info{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",role_name=~"${role:regex}"}

carla_vehicle_control_reverse{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",actor_id=~"${actor:regex}"} * on (job, instance, episode_id, actor_id) group_left(role_name, blueprint_id) carla_vehicle_info{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",role_name=~"${role:regex}"}

panels.title: Hand brake & reverse

panels.description: Exporter build version, source revision, and Go toolchain version. The metric has value 1; labels contain the information. Different binaries can expose different runtime metric sets.
panels.title: Exporter build

panels.description: Wall-clock time since the exporter process started, calculated from process_start_time_seconds. It resets on exporter restart and differs from CARLA server or world uptime.
panels.title: Process uptime

panels.description: Go runtime version from go_info. The metric value is always 1; the version is carried in a label. Go/runtime panels require the standard Go collector metrics.
panels.title: Go runtime

panels.description: CARLA collection duration is measured inside the exporter. Prometheus scrape duration includes the full scrape path, response transfer, and processing. Both are wall-clock seconds and should be interpreted against the configured scrape timeout.
panels.title: Collection & scrape duration

panels.description: CPU time consumed per wall-clock second, in CPU cores. A value of 1 means one fully utilized logical CPU; a multithreaded process can exceed 1. Rates use Grafana's rate interval and require multiple samples.
panels.title: CPU usage

panels.description: Resident memory is physical memory currently resident for the exporter process. Virtual memory is its mapped address space and can be much larger; the two are not interchangeable measures of memory pressure.
panels.title: Process memory

panels.description: Goroutines are Go tasks, OS threads are runtime threads, and GOMAXPROCS limits simultaneous execution of Go code. They measure different aspects of concurrency and need not match.
panels.title: Go concurrency

panels.description: Samples scraped before and after metric relabeling, plus series newly added during a scrape. New-series counts are per scrape, not the total number of active series. Changes can reflect actor churn or label changes.
panels.title: Scrape samples

panels.description: Open file descriptors compared with the process limit. The limit uses the right-hand axis so the open count remains readable; compare numeric values rather than the apparent line heights.
panels.title: Open file descriptors

panels.description: Receive/transmit rates from the process network-namespace counters. Scope depends on deployment: with host networking they include host traffic; in a private container network namespace they include that namespace. These are not exporter-only application bytes.
panels.title: Network namespace traffic

panels.description: Exported GC pause quantiles describe the runtime summary, not percentiles calculated over the selected dashboard range. Mean pause is rate(sum) / rate(count) over Grafana's rate interval. It can be unavailable when there are no GC events.
panels.title: GC pause duration

panels.description: Heap alloc is bytes in allocated objects; inuse is heap spans in use; idle is unused spans; released is idle memory returned to the OS; sys is heap memory obtained from the OS. These overlap and must not be summed.
panels.title: Heap memory

panels.description: Allocated object memory, total memory obtained from the OS by the Go runtime, and the next GC heap target. Reserved runtime memory is not the same as process RSS or a container memory limit.
panels.title: Memory allocator

panels.description: Rate of cumulative bytes allocated by the Go runtime, including allocations that have already been freed. This is allocation throughput, not net memory growth.
panels.title: Allocation rate

panels.description: Rates of heap object allocations and frees. Differences indicate changes in live object count over the measurement interval, not necessarily a leak.
panels.title: Object allocation & frees

panels.description: Number of allocated heap objects currently tracked by the Go runtime. Use its trend together with allocation rates and heap memory to investigate retention.
panels.title: Heap objects

panels.description: Rate of completed garbage collections, in collections per second. A period without GC can produce zero; absent metrics or insufficient samples produce no data.
panels.title: Garbage collections

panels.description: Wall-clock time since the most recent garbage collection. This calculation depends on host clock time. A longer interval can simply mean low allocation activity.
panels.title: Time since last GC

panels.description: Stack memory in use versus memory obtained from the OS for stacks. These are Go runtime stack metrics, not the process virtual address-space size.
panels.title: Stack memory

panels.description: Runtime bookkeeping memory for profiling hash buckets, GC metadata, allocator caches, spans, and other allocations. Some values are in-use memory and others are reserved; they overlap and are not an additive total.
panels.title: Runtime metadata memory

panels.description: Configured GOGC percentage: the GC heap growth target relative to the live heap after the previous collection. This is a tuning setting, not the fraction of time spent in GC.
panels.title: GC target

panels.description: Go runtime soft memory limit (GOMEMLIMIT). Unlimited denotes the runtime's effectively unbounded default. It is not a hard process or container limit and does not cover all memory outside the Go runtime.
panels.title: Go memory limit

panels.description: Maximum virtual memory address-space limit exposed by the process collector. Unlimited denotes an effectively unbounded limit. This is not a resident-memory or container-memory limit.
panels.title: Virtual memory limit

list.description: Prometheus datasource containing the CARLA exporter metrics. Configure its scrape interval to match the Prometheus job for reliable rate windows.
list.label: Datasource
list.name: datasource

list.description: Scrape job discovered from the exporter's build-info metric; the job name is not prescribed.
list.label: Job
list.name: job

list.description: One exporter target. World values describe this instance; select another instance to inspect another CARLA server.
list.label: Instance
list.name: instance

list.description: Filter vehicle panels by role_name. Roles may be empty or shared by multiple actors; world totals are not filtered.
list.label: Vehicle role
list.name: role

list.description: Filter vehicle panels by actor ID. Actor IDs can be reused across CARLA episodes; telemetry is joined by episode as well.
list.label: Actor ID
list.name: actor

title: CARLA Exporter
